# Plan: SPE round r01 for the "triage" agent

This is round r01. Nothing exists yet, so this round builds the first agent and its eval harness, then measures it. The plan below is the prediction. Nothing is written to disk until you approve it.

Default chosen: I assume the 40 tickets and the support lead's labels will be placed at `data/tickets.jsonl` and `data/labels.jsonl`. If they are not there, I halt and ask you for the path.

## 1. Specify

### Requirement table (goes to `spe/spec/spec.md` under "Round r01")

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | The agent assigns exactly one category from billing, bug, how-to, account, outage. | User: "triage tickets correctly" | `grade_category_exact` against the support lead's label |
| R2 | The agent assigns exactly one priority from P1, P2, P3, P4. | User: "triage tickets correctly" | `grade_priority_exact` and `grade_priority_within1` |
| R3 | The agent never misses a P1 ticket. | Decision D1 (default) | `grade_p1_recall` must equal 1.00 |
| R4 | The agent drafts a first reply that addresses the issue and invents no facts, refunds, policies, or ETAs. | Project description | `judge_reply` with a frozen 4-point rubric |
| R5 | Every output matches the JSON schema `{category, priority, reply, rationale}`. | Decision D2 (default) | `grade_schema` |
| R6 | The cost per ticket stays at or below $0.010. | User: "cheaply", with threshold from D3 (default) | `cost_from_usage` from API token counts and a price table |
| R7 | The agent prompt contains no ticket or label from the 40-ticket eval set. | Decision D4 (default) | Leak scan of every assembled prompt |
| R8 | The winning configuration is the cheapest one that meets R1 to R5. | User: "correctly and cheaply" | Rule applied in the results summary |

### Decisions and logged defaults (goes to `spe/spec/disagreements.md`)

| ID | Decision | Default I will use | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Is a missed P1 the worst failure? | Yes. P1 recall must be 1.00. | You |
| D2 | Output format | Structured output with a fixed JSON schema. | Claude (default) |
| D3 | What "cheap" means | $0.010 per ticket or less. Correctness targets are category accuracy of 0.85 or more and priority exact accuracy of 0.65 or more. | You |
| D4 | Few-shot examples | None from the 40 tickets. With only 40 tickets, every ticket stays in the test set. | Claude (default) |
| D5 | Priority definitions | I draft P1 to P4 definitions in `triage/rubric.md`. P1 means an outage or data loss for many customers. P4 means a question with no business impact. The support lead should confirm them. | You and the support lead |
| D6 | Models | The current Sonnet and Haiku model IDs, checked against the Anthropic models docs at build time and recorded in `triage/models.json`. The judge is the current Opus model. | Claude (default) |

## 2. Predict

### Configurations (one change each from the base)

| Config | Model | Prompt | Change from C1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| C0 control | None | Always predicts the most common category and priority in the labels | Baseline, no model |
| C1 base | Sonnet | Rubric prompt with category and priority definitions | None |
| C2 cheap | Haiku | Same as C1 | Model only |
| C3 no-rubric | Sonnet | Label names only, no definitions | Rubric removed |

### Numbers

Each cell is a point and a band. A hit means the measured value falls inside the band. One ticket out of 40 is 0.025, so bands are wide on purpose.

| Metric | Grader check | C0 | C1 | C2 | C3 | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Category accuracy | `grade_category_exact` | 0.30 ± 0.10 | 0.85 ± 0.07 | 0.80 ± 0.08 | 0.78 ± 0.08 | Most categories are clear from the wording. Bug versus outage and account versus billing are the main confusions, and the rubric reduces them. |
| Priority exact accuracy | `grade_priority_exact` | 0.40 ± 0.10 | 0.60 ± 0.10 | 0.52 ± 0.10 | 0.45 ± 0.10 | Priority follows the support lead's unwritten policy. My drafted rubric will only partly match it. |
| Priority within one level | `grade_priority_within1` | 0.75 ± 0.10 | 0.92 ± 0.05 | 0.88 ± 0.06 | 0.85 ± 0.07 | Most priority misses will be off by one level, not two. |
| P1 recall | `grade_p1_recall` | 0.00 ± 0.00 | 0.80 ± 0.20 | 0.70 ± 0.20 | 0.70 ± 0.20 | There are likely only 4 to 6 P1 tickets, so one miss moves recall by 0.15 to 0.25. |
| Schema validity | `grade_schema` | 1.00 ± 0.00 | 1.00 ± 0.02 | 1.00 ± 0.02 | 1.00 ± 0.02 | Structured output enforces the schema. |
| Reply pass rate | `judge_reply` | n/a | 0.85 ± 0.10 | 0.75 ± 0.10 | 0.83 ± 0.10 | The rubric affects labels more than replies. A smaller model invents details in replies more often. |
| Label agreement across 3 trials | `grade_consistency` | 1.00 ± 0.00 | 0.93 ± 0.05 | 0.88 ± 0.06 | 0.88 ± 0.06 | Rubric definitions make repeated runs pick the same label. |
| Cost per ticket (USD) | `cost_from_usage` | 0.000 | 0.012 ± 0.004 | 0.004 ± 0.0015 | 0.010 ± 0.004 | About 2,300 input and 400 output tokens per ticket at list prices. The C3 prompt is shorter. These are estimates until measured. |

Overall prediction: no configuration meets every target in r01. C1 meets the category target but misses priority and P1 recall. C2 is the only configuration under the cost cap. The likely r02 change is a priority rubric confirmed by the support lead.

`same_as_last_round` is `null` for every number because this is the first round.

## 3. Evaluate

### Build (after the predict commit)

1. Write `triage/agent.py`. It makes one API call per ticket with no tools and returns the JSON schema from R5.
2. Write `triage/prompt.md`, `triage/rubric.md`, and `triage/models.json`.
3. Write the graders in `spe/evals/harness/graders.py`. Code checks come first. The only judge is `judge_reply`. Its rubric has 4 points: it addresses the actual issue, it invents no facts or promises, it asks for missing information when needed, and its tone is professional. The judge sees the ticket and the reply. It does not see the config name.
4. Write the Workflow script `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js`. It holds the round in one `ROUND = "r01"` constant.

### Gates before launch

| Gate | Pass condition |
|---|---|
| Grader selftest | The labels file scores 1.00 on every code check. Empty outputs score 0 and fail the schema check. Rotated labels score below 0.30. |
| Control | No last round exists. C0 is graded instead and must land near the label distribution. |
| Leak check | Answer files sit in `data/labels.jsonl` and `spe/predictions/`. The trial process never opens either path. A scan of every assembled prompt finds no label text. Any trial that fails the scan is voided. |
| Dry run | 3 cells (C1 on tickets 1 to 3) run end to end and grade without errors. |

### Workflow arguments

```json
{
  "ROUND": "r01",
  "configs": ["C0-control", "C1-base", "C2-cheap", "C3-norubric"],
  "tickets": "data/tickets.jsonl",
  "trials_per_ticket": 3,
  "split_cell_extra_trials_cap": 2,
  "spend_cap_usd": 25,
  "per_config_cap_usd": 8,
  "dry_run_cells": 3
}
```

### Run steps

1. Run 40 tickets × 3 trials for C1, C2, and C3. C0 runs once in code.
2. Grade with code checks, then run `judge_reply`.
3. When the 3 trials of a ticket disagree on a label, add up to 2 more trials for that ticket.
4. Skip any trial that would cross a spend cap. Log each skip to `spe/evals/runs/r01/skips.jsonl`.
5. Run failure analysis. It groups wrong answers into F-numbered failure types.
6. Run a completeness critic. It checks that every cell was graded and that every predicted number has a measured value.

### Cost estimate (not measured)

Agent calls: 360 base trials plus up to 80 extra. That comes to about $6 at estimated list prices. Judge calls on Opus come to about $8. The expected total is about $14. The hard cap is $25.

### Halt conditions

I halt and report if a spend cap is hit, the answer key leaks, a grader fails its selftest, or a decision only you can make blocks the run.

## 4. Files and commits

Each step gets one local commit. I will not push and I will not push tags.

| Step | Files | Commit message |
|---|---|---|
| Specify | `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r01.md` (your prompt, verbatim), `spe/spec/spec.md`, `spe/spec/disagreements.md` | `SPE r01 specify` |
| Predict | `spe/plans/r01.md`, `spe/predictions/r01.yaml` (starts with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.`, author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode") | `SPE r01 predict: C1 0.85 category, C2 only config under cost cap` |
| Build | `triage/` | `SPE r01 build: triage agent C0 to C3` |
| Harness | `spe/evals/harness/` | `SPE r01 evaluate (harness)` |
| Results | `spe/evals/runs/r01/` | `SPE r01 evaluate (results): <headline>` |
| Learn | `spe/prediction-log.md`, `spe/failures.md`, the "Proposed for round r02" table in `spe/spec/spec.md`, `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` (`status: draft`), `spe/README.md` | `SPE r01 learn`, then tag `spe-r01` |

The learn step starts when the Workflow completion notice arrives, not when the Workflow launches. The prediction log will quote each missed Why and name the wrong assumption. It will also say plainly if C0 or the naive guess beat my numbers.

## Decisions for you

If you approve without changes, the defaults above apply.

1. D1: Should P1 recall have to be 1.00?
2. D3: Are $0.010 per ticket, 0.85 category accuracy, and 0.65 priority accuracy the right targets?
3. D5: Can the support lead review `triage/rubric.md` before r02?
